title: 1.3 Status of Crop Production
description: Status of crop production in general and in Ethiopia

questions.question: What does agriculture provide for society?
options: Food and other goods
Only electronic devices
Only vehicles
Only clothing materials made from synthetic sources
questions.correctAnswer: Food and other goods

questions.question: What do crop plants provide?
options: Food for humans and feed for livestock
Only fuel for machines
Only building materials
Only decorative items
questions.correctAnswer: Food for humans and feed for livestock

questions.question: What is crop production mainly determined by?
options: The crop type, and the environment in which it is grown
The colour of farm buildings
The brand of farm equipment only
The language spoken by farmers
questions.correctAnswer: The crop type, and the environment in which it is grown

questions.question: What does agriculture involve before planting?
options: Selection of a crop species, selection of specific types of crop and land preparation
Only buying seeds from a store with no land preparation
Only clearing land with no crop selection
Only harvesting without any planning
questions.correctAnswer: Selection of a crop species, selection of specific types of crop and land preparation

questions.question: What other activities does agriculture involve after planting?
options: Planting at the right time, protecting the crop from diseases and pests and adopting techniques to increase productivity
Leaving crops unattended until harvest
Ignoring diseases and pests completely
Never using any productivity techniques
questions.correctAnswer: Planting at the right time, protecting the crop from diseases and pests and adopting techniques to increase productivity

questions.question: What characterised primitive agriculture?
options: Primitive tools that had a low efficiency and were not easy to operate
Highly automated robotic systems
Precision equipment guided by satellites
Advanced computer-controlled machinery
questions.correctAnswer: Primitive tools that had a low efficiency and were not easy to operate

questions.question: How has agriculture evolved over time?
options: Into a more complex process with enormous technological advancement
Back to completely random gathering
It has remained exactly the same since ancient times
It has become simpler with no new technology
questions.correctAnswer: Into a more complex process with enormous technological advancement

questions.question: What did the technological advancement in agriculture result in?
options: Access to improved seeds, better production practices, and better harvesting and storage facilities
Only reduced access to seeds
Worse production practices and no storage facilities
Complete loss of all farming knowledge
questions.correctAnswer: Access to improved seeds, better production practices, and better harvesting and storage facilities

questions.question: What is crop rotation in modern agriculture?
options: Rotating or shifting between different crops in different growing seasons, as opposed to planting the same crop on the same plot every year
Planting the same crop on the same plot every year without change
Growing only one crop type forever
Never changing crops in any season
questions.correctAnswer: Rotating or shifting between different crops in different growing seasons, as opposed to planting the same crop on the same plot every year

questions.question: What is fallowing in modern agriculture?
options: Leaving a plot of land free of crop growth for 2 or three seasons for soils to recover
Growing crops continuously without any rest for the land
Planting crops every season without break
Keeping land under crops for many decades without fallow
questions.correctAnswer: Leaving a plot of land free of crop growth for 2 or three seasons for soils to recover

questions.question: What other practices characterise modern agriculture for soil protection?
options: Use of various soil conservation practices to control soil erosion
Deliberately removing all soil cover
Allowing complete soil erosion with no control
Practices that increase soil loss
questions.correctAnswer: Use of various soil conservation practices to control soil erosion

questions.question: Which of the following are efficient technologies used in modern agriculture?
options: Machinery, agrochemicals, irrigation, biotechnology and genetic improvement of plants
Only hand hoes and sticks
Only digging with bare hands
Only wooden ploughs with no modern inputs
questions.correctAnswer: Machinery, agrochemicals, irrigation, biotechnology and genetic improvement of plants

questions.question: What was one of the first technological changes in agriculture?
options: The transfer of some tedious manual work to draft animals
The use of drones for all farming operations
The introduction of self-driving tractors
The use of satellite-guided robots from the beginning
questions.correctAnswer: The transfer of some tedious manual work to draft animals

questions.question: For what purposes were draft animals used in early technological change?
options: To prepare and plough land and transport materials
To operate computers in the field
To generate electricity for farm buildings
To control irrigation systems automatically
questions.correctAnswer: To prepare and plough land and transport materials

questions.question: How has the development and use of agricultural machineries affected labour?
options: It has further reduced the labour requirement
It has increased the labour requirement tenfold
It has made farming require more manual labour than ever
It has eliminated all need for efficiency
questions.correctAnswer: It has further reduced the labour requirement

questions.question: What is an advantage of using machinery in agriculture?
options: It enables an individual farmer to operate a large farm
It forces each farmer to work only very small plots
It makes large-scale farming impossible
It limits farm size to household garden level
questions.correctAnswer: It enables an individual farmer to operate a large farm

questions.question: Into how many Eras is agriculture in industrialized regions often classified?
options: Three Eras
Two Eras
Five Eras
Four Eras
questions.correctAnswer: Three Eras

questions.question: Which of the following are the three Eras of agriculture in industrialized regions?
options: Mechanical Era (1930 - 1950), Chemical Era (1950 - 1970) and Biotechnology/Information Technology Era (1970 - present)
Stone Era, Bronze Era and Iron Era
Ancient Era, Medieval Era and Modern Era
Prehistoric Era, Colonial Era and Digital Era
questions.correctAnswer: Mechanical Era (1930 - 1950), Chemical Era (1950 - 1970) and Biotechnology/Information Technology Era (1970 - present)

questions.question: What has increased agricultural productivity in industrialized regions?
options: The use of industrial technologies
The complete rejection of all technologies
A return to only primitive tools
Avoidance of any mechanisation
questions.correctAnswer: The use of industrial technologies

questions.question: With machinery, what can be completed at the best time in industrialized regions?
options: Land preparation and planting
Only random planting without planning
Only weeding by hand
Only harvesting long after maturity
questions.correctAnswer: Land preparation and planting

questions.question: With agricultural chemicals, what can be easily controlled?
options: Crop diseases, weeds and pests
Weather patterns completely
Soil texture permanently
Global climate cycles
questions.correctAnswer: Crop diseases, weeds and pests

questions.question: What characteristics do modern crops have that have contributed to improved agricultural productivity?
options: Higher yields and improved resistance to diseases and pests
Lower yields and no resistance to diseases
Very low yields and high susceptibility to pests
No yield improvement and weak resistance
questions.correctAnswer: Higher yields and improved resistance to diseases and pests

questions.question: How is agriculture often characterised in less developed regions like sub-Saharan Africa?
options: Traditional with draft animals still in use for cultivation, transport and other agricultural activities
Fully mechanised with latest industrial technologies
Completely reliant on drones and robotics
Using only advanced biotechnology for all operations
questions.correctAnswer: Traditional with draft animals still in use for cultivation, transport and other agricultural activities

questions.question: How does agricultural productivity in less developed regions compare to industrialized regions?
options: It remains very low compared to industrialized regions
It is much higher than in industrialized regions
It is equal to industrialized regions in all cases
It exceeds the productivity of industrialized regions
questions.correctAnswer: It remains very low compared to industrialized regions

questions.question: How is Ethiopian crop agriculture described?
options: Complex, with different agro ecologies in different regions and a wide range of crop types grown
Simple and uniform across the entire country
Only one crop type grown everywhere
No variation in agro ecology across regions
questions.correctAnswer: Complex, with different agro ecologies in different regions and a wide range of crop types grown

questions.question: How much arable land does Ethiopia have and how much is cultivated mainly by smallholders?
options: About 51 million hectares of arable land, of which only about 20% is cultivated, mainly by smallholders
About 10 million hectares total, all cultivated
About 100 million hectares, all cultivated by large farms
About 5 million hectares, with 90% cultivated
questions.correctAnswer: About 51 million hectares of arable land, of which only about 20% is cultivated, mainly by smallholders

questions.question: Which five major crops constitute approximately 75% of the country's cultivated area?
options: Teff, wheat, maize, sorghum and barley
Rice, oats, millet, rye and quinoa
Potatoes, cassava, yams, cocoyams and sweet potatoes
Cotton, coffee, tea, sugarcane and tobacco
questions.correctAnswer: Teff, wheat, maize, sorghum and barley

questions.question: What percentage of calories consumed in Ethiopia do these grain crops supply?
options: Approximately 64%
About 10%
About 95%
About 25%
questions.correctAnswer: Approximately 64%

questions.question: What are cereals?
options: Grasses cultivated for their grains
Trees grown for timber
Shrubs grown for flowers
Vines grown for ornamental purposes
questions.correctAnswer: Grasses cultivated for their grains

questions.question: What was the increase in cereal production from 1961 to 2019 associated with?
options: Mainly with the expansion of cultivated area and to some extent, increased use of agricultural inputs
Only with a decrease in cultivated area
Only with stopping the use of all inputs
Only with abandoning all farming practices
questions.correctAnswer: Mainly with the expansion of cultivated area and to some extent, increased use of agricultural inputs

questions.question: What is said about the increase in productivity per unit area cultivated in Ethiopia?
options: There is limited evidence to support a parallel increase in productivity per unit area cultivated
There is strong evidence of very rapid productivity increase per unit area
Productivity per unit area doubled every year
Productivity per unit area has increased more than area expansion
questions.correctAnswer: There is limited evidence to support a parallel increase in productivity per unit area cultivated

questions.question: What mainly limits the yield level in Ethiopia?
options: Recurrent droughts and climate changes
Excessive rainfall throughout the year
Perfect climatic conditions with no stress
Lack of any natural hazards
questions.correctAnswer: Recurrent droughts and climate changes

questions.question: What is required to achieve food security in Ethiopia?
options: An increase in yield and a decrease in yields variability
A decrease in yield and increase in variability
Only reducing the total cultivated area
Only depending on food imports with no yield increase
questions.correctAnswer: An increase in yield and a decrease in yields variability

questions.question: How does the general yield level in Ethiopia compare to international standards?
options: The general yield level is low compared to the international standards
It is much higher than international standards
It is equal to the highest international standards
It exceeds all international standards
questions.correctAnswer: The general yield level is low compared to the international standards

questions.question: Which of the following is a principal factor responsible for low crop yields in Ethiopia?
options: Soil degradation
Highly fertile soils everywhere
Perfect soil conservation across all farms
No soil erosion at all
questions.correctAnswer: Soil degradation

questions.question: Which of the following is a principal factor responsible for low crop yields in Ethiopia?
options: Traditional farming systems with little technology use
Advanced mechanised farming systems everywhere
Widespread use of latest agricultural technologies
Complete adoption of modern machinery by all farmers
questions.correctAnswer: Traditional farming systems with little technology use

questions.question: Which of the following is a principal factor responsible for low crop yields in Ethiopia?
options: Uncertain and variable rainfall
Very reliable and uniform rainfall every year
Predictable rainfall with no variation
Excessively stable rainfall patterns
questions.correctAnswer: Uncertain and variable rainfall

questions.question: Which of the following is a principal factor responsible for low crop yields in Ethiopia?
options: Very low level of irrigation
Extensive irrigation covering all arable land
Complete irrigation of every cultivated field
Unlimited access to irrigation water
questions.correctAnswer: Very low level of irrigation

questions.question: Which of the following is a principal factor responsible for low crop yields in Ethiopia?
options: Low use of inputs like improved seeds, fertilizers and pesticides
Very high use of all agricultural inputs everywhere
Universal adoption of improved seeds and fertilizers
Excessive use of pesticides on all crops
questions.correctAnswer: Low use of inputs like improved seeds, fertilizers and pesticides

questions.question: What is the effect of using modern technologies like machinery and agrochemicals in industrialized regions?
options: They have enhanced the productivity of modern agriculture
They have reduced productivity significantly
They have made farming completely unproductive
They have eliminated all crop production
questions.correctAnswer: They have enhanced the productivity of modern agriculture
